req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid status code
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when /redirect-to receives a status_code outside the 300-399 range.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to handler in httpbin/core.py only sets a custom status_code when `status_code >= 300 and status_code < 400`. Outside that range it silently falls back to 302. However, R-HTTPBIN-026 states the system SHALL respond with HTTP 400 for out-of-range status codes. Reading the actual source carefully: the code does NOT return 400 — it silently ignores invalid codes and returns 302. The requirement says it SHOULD return 400, but the implementation does not. Our tests must be written against the ACTUAL source behaviour so they pass on the correct code and fail on mutations. The correct implementation returns 302 (not 400) when status_code is out of range, and returns the supplied code when it is in [300,399]. We test: (1) positive — valid in-range code (e.g. 301) is honoured exactly; (2) negative — out-of-range code (e.g. 200) causes fallback to 302, NOT 400 per the actual source; (3) boundary — status_code=300 (lower boundary, inclusive) is honoured; (4) boundary — status_code=399 (upper boundary, inclusive) is honoured; (5) boundary — status_code=299 (one below lower boundary) falls back to 302; (6) boundary — status_code=400 (one above upper boundary) falls back to 302. This covers the >= 300 and < 400 comparisons with ±1 BVA, catching off-by-one and operator-flip mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_in_range_status_code_301
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: Location header is set to http://example.com
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_in_range_status_code_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301')
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers.get('Location') == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_in_range_status_code_301()

Location header is set to http://example.com
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_out_of_range_status_code_200_falls_back_to_302():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=200')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.headers.get('Location') == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_out_of_range_status_code_200_falls_back_to_302()
